data.summary: The 12‑week plan uses the student’s 2 hours per week to build a solid foundation, prioritize the weak Unit 7 and Unit 8 early, and then rotate through the remaining units. Each week focuses on a small set of topic codes with a concrete practice task. The final two weeks are reserved for mixed review and timed free‑response practice to simulate the exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce differential equations basics and slope fields
tasks: Read the textbook section on modeling with differential equations (7.1).
Do 5 practice problems creating differential equations from word prompts.
Sketch slope fields for 3 given differential equations (7.3).

weeks.focus: Verify solutions and interpret slope fields
tasks: Solve 4 differential equations and check each solution by substitution (7.2).
Answer 3 conceptual questions about what slope fields reveal about solution behavior (7.4).
Compute the average value of 3 functions on given intervals (8.1).
Use integrals to find position from a velocity function and velocity from an acceleration function (8.2).

weeks.focus: Further integration applications and area between curves
tasks: Set up and evaluate 3 accumulation‑function problems in applied contexts (8.3).
Find the area between two curves for 2 pairs of functions (8.4).
Watch a short video on limit definition and write the limit notation for 5 examples (1.1, 1.2).
Apply algebraic limit properties to evaluate 6 limits (1.5).
Calculate average and instantaneous rates of change for 3 motion scenarios (2.1).
Differentiate 5 functions using the definition and power rule (2.2, 2.5).
Differentiate 4 composite functions using the chain rule (3.1).
Solve 3 implicit differentiation problems and check your results (3.2).

weeks.focus: Applications of differentiation – motion and rates
tasks: Given position functions, find velocity and acceleration and interpret the results (4.2).
Complete 3 related‑rates problems from physics contexts (4.4).

weeks.focus: Mean Value and Extreme Value Theorems
tasks: State the Mean Value Theorem for 2 functions and verify its hypotheses (5.1).
Identify critical points and classify extrema for 4 functions using EVT (5.2).

weeks.focus: First derivative test and increasing/decreasing intervals
tasks: Determine intervals of increase/decrease for 3 functions (5.3).
Apply the First Derivative Test to locate and classify local extrema for 3 additional functions (5.4).

weeks.focus: Mixed review – core concepts and weak units
tasks: Do a 10‑minute timed set: 2 limit problems, 2 differential‑equation modeling tasks, and 2 average‑value integrals.
Review notes on slope fields and sketch one from memory.

weeks.focus: Full‑length timed practice and final review
tasks: Complete a 30‑minute free‑response practice set covering FTC, interpretation of derivatives, and first‑derivative test.
Mark answers against the scoring guide and note any remaining weak spots.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, simulate exam conditions with timed free‑response questions, then spend any remaining minutes reviewing the specific errors you made. Keep a cheat‑sheet of key formulas (FTC, chain rule, DE solution steps) for quick reference the day before the exam.
